parsed.explanation: The jurisdiction is governed by national rules with no local exemption. Positive signals—no criminalisation, long-standing legality, anti-discrimination law, marriage equality, and local community infrastructure—are mainly climate or resident-facing and do not neutralise custody exposure. The dominant documented traveler-facing risk is prison placement: trans women are placed according to identity documents, often in male facilities where they are threatened, and the national detention watchdog found persistent serious violations, with recommendations not changing practice. Any outed trans visitor taken into local custody faces this same regime. Island-specific violence and enforcement data are absent, so silence is not safety. Local acceptance cannot override state-run custody rules. This fits Elevated Risk, similar to documented birth-sex or marker-based custody practice with partial legal protections and ineffective recourse.
